new: verify the step proof under the constant step verifier data, re-register from_pis(step public inputs) unchanged, assert the built common data equals the cyclic common data
spans.note: Handwritten local semantics; no source/compiler refinement. This wrapper adds NO constraints of its own: it forwards the step circuit's public inputs verbatim, which is what makes the step's own conditionally-verified previous proof a proof of this same circuit. That forwarding is what lets the Chain inductive treat a continued step's prevPis as itself reachable. The common-data equality assert and try_build_with_options are build-time plonky2 behaviour and are not modeled.

spans.note: Handwritten local semantics; no source/compiler refinement. This is the ConsumerVdPin discharge point modeled here: a chain proof accepted by verify demonstrably declares this circuit's verifier data in its public inputs, and the cyclic check runs first so a proof with a foreign declared vd is rejected without reaching plonky2. Nothing forces any OTHER consumer (block_step.rs) to perform the same check.

boundaries.name: plonky2_refinement
boundaries.obligation: The handwritten gate equations (CircuitGates, WrapGates), the builder/prover/verifier programs and the registered public-input vector must be linked to actual plonky2 compilation, proving and verification; none of that lowering is discharged here.

boundaries.name: hash_opacity
boundaries.obligation: Environment.keccakWords (plonky2_keccak solidity_keccak256 over u32 words), poseidonWords (PoseidonHashOut::hash_inputs_u64) and twoToOne (the Poseidon 2-to-1 of the incremental deposit tree) are opaque callbacks. No collision resistance, preimage resistance or injectivity is assumed or proved, so equal accumulator values never imply equal deposit sequences.

boundaries.name: proof_soundness
boundaries.obligation: Environment.proofAccepted vd pis is an opaque Bool. 'accepted implies produced by a gate-satisfying witness' is encoded as the Chain inductive premise, never proved; plonky2/FRI soundness is out of scope.

boundaries.name: consumer_vd_pin
boundaries.obligation: On the initial step new_pis.vd is a free virtual verifier data (theorem initial_step_vd_unconstrained) and every continued step forwards it unchanged (chain_declares_single_vd). Only a consumer pins it to the real chain verifier data: DepositHashChainCircuit::verify -> check_cyclic_proof_verifier_data (modeled as chain_verify_pins_declared_vd) or block_step.rs add_proof_target_and_conditionally_verify_cyclic, which is outside the modeled files and must be audited there.

boundaries.name: field_and_gadget_lowering
boundaries.obligation: Goldilocks arithmetic, split_le, range_check, select, the keccak and Poseidon gadgets, DepositMerkleProofTarget and from_pis slicing are modeled as Nat equations over lists. Their circuit lowering, and in particular that split_le(prev_count, 63) is what bounds the previous count below 2^63, is assumed.

boundaries.name: vd_canonicity
boundaries.obligation: vd_from_pis_slice / vd_from_pis_slice_target read verifier-data field elements from u64 public inputs with no canonicity check; verifier-data words are carried as an opaque List Nat and compared only for equality.

boundaries.name: common_data_fixpoint
boundaries.obligation: new asserts data.common == generate_cd() and that try_build_with_options succeeded, i.e. that the circuit built here really is the cyclic circuit whose common data the step circuit was built against. That fixpoint (and the num_public_inputs overwrite in generate_cd being consistent with the registered vector) is a plonky2 build-time property the model assumes rather than proves.

boundaries.name: step_vd_is_constant
boundaries.obligation: add_proof_target_and_verify embeds the deposit-step verifier data as a CONSTANT, so this wrapper only ever accepts genuine deposit-step proofs. That constancy is a property of the imported helper and is assumed, not modeled.
